The only feature that gives rather than records, so it shares the recap's voice — the app speaking, not the app logging. A sheet off the row that already sits on Today. Nothing is saved by asking; back always lands on Today.

Drawn in the Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup` as `Advice.dc.html`. Seven screens, four of which are the honest states — they are the reason anyone believes the other three.

## The entry point — recommendation

**Keep the row on Today.** Doc 19's routing table already lists `What should I eat?` as a sheet reached from "the suggestion row on Today", and doc 12 §5 already specifies the row with the remaining budget on its right. It is drawn in `4a`, `4b` and `4c`.

The two alternatives were considered and rejected:

* **A button under the ring** puts a second accent-weight control directly above ＋ LOG FOOD. At the moment of hunger — which is also the moment of logging — the primary action must be unambiguous. Two buttons competing there is the one place this feature can do real damage.
* **An action in the ＋ menu** buries a hunger-moment feature behind a capture affordance. Wrong mental model: ＋ means *I ate something*, not *what should I eat*.

The row wins on placement as much as anything: it sits immediately under the protein and fiber tiles, so the question and the numbers that answer it are read in one glance.

### The row's three states

| State | Trailing text | Behaviour |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Default | `740 · 82P LEFT` | Accent. Context, not cost |
| Low | `2 ASKS LEFT` | Dim. Count replaces the budget at two remaining |
| Spent | `NONE LEFT TODAY` | Muted, hairline border, still tappable — opens 9f |

The cost signal is deliberately absent until it matters. A permanent counter makes an occasional feature feel metered from day one; showing nothing at all means the quota state arrives as a surprise. Appearing at two is the compromise.

## States table

| State | Header | Tag line | Cards | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Loading | `Reading your day` | Indeterminate accent bar | Four context lines, three resolved and one pending | Names what it knows: budget, meals so far, time of day. Footer states 1 of 12 daily requests |
| Results | `Three that fit` | `740 KCAL · 82P · 11F LEFT · 7:12 PM` in accent | 3 suggestions | Name, macros in accent mono, one line of reasoning |
| Already over | `You're past the calories` | `160 KCAL OVER · 18P · 7F STILL SHORT` in orange | 2 light options + `Or stop here` | Third card carries an orange border and the tag `THE HONEST ANSWER` |
| Hard constraint | `This is a tight one` | `210 KCAL · 74P LEFT · 9:24 PM` in dim | 2 options + `You won't close 74g tonight` | Accent border on the third card, **not** orange |
| Quota reached | `That's the last one today` | `12 OF 12 AI REQUESTS USED` · `RESETS MIDNIGHT` | A full progress bar, then a `STILL FREE, STILL YOURS` card | Ends on LOG BY HAND as the accent action |
| Nothing logged | `What to start with` | `NOTHING LOGGED YET · WORKING FROM YOUR TARGETS AND THE CLOCK, NOT YOUR DAY` | 3 first-meal suggestions | Footer: log one meal and the next answer gets sharper |

Every card is the same object: name at 15/700, macros at 11.5px accent mono, reasoning at 13px dim.

## Decisions

**Orange stays reserved.** Doc 12's rule is that orange means calories over target and nothing else. `9d` uses it because that is literally what it is. `9e` — a hard constraint, not an overage — uses accent instead. A tight protein target is not a failure and must not borrow the failure colour.

**The third card is never filler.** In every honest state the third slot carries the thing the model would rather not say: *stop here*, *you won't close it*, *this is a guess*. Keeping three cards everywhere means the honest answer occupies a suggestion's visual weight rather than a disclaimer's.

The quota state gives something back. `9f` still shows what's left, because that number is subtraction and never needed a model. Ending on *logging by hand still works* keeps the failure from reading as a locked door, and LOG BY HAND rather than CLOSE takes the accent slot — dismissal should not be the primary action.

**Advice exists before the first entry, but says what it is.** Hiding the row would be tidier and less honest. Reframed as *what to start with*, working from targets and the clock, with the limitation stated in the header rather than buried.

**The loading state is the cost signal.** It names the context it is using and states `1 OF YOUR 12 DAILY REQUESTS`. That is where the deliberateness of the ask lives — not in a permanent badge on Today.

**Pre-fill is one attribute away.** Each suggestion is already a self-contained card with a name and three macros — exactly the payload a manual entry needs. Making it tappable later adds a chevron and no layout change.

## Gaps and open questions

The daily quota number is invented. `12` is used throughout because doc 12's settings screen shows a quota bar without a figure. It needs to be a real number before this ships, and the same number has to appear in Settings, in `7h`, and here.

Nine of twelve went to photos. `9f` names the split to make the shared pool concrete. If the backend doesn't track per-feature usage, that line has to go — it is the one piece of copy here that asserts data that may not exist.

**Advice is never shown on a past day.** The row is drawn out of `4d`, which is correct, but nothing states the rule. Worth writing down: advice is a today-only feature.

**No repeat-suppression is visible.** The brief says the server avoids suggesting chicken twice and avoids recent-day repetition. `9b` claims it in a loading line. Nothing in the results confirms it happened, and there is no way for a user to say *not this again*.

**The three suggestions have no provenance.** They are model output presented in the same visual language as the deterministic recap layers, which are explicitly labelled as arithmetic. Doc 17 makes a virtue of separating computed facts from generated advice. This sheet should probably carry the same distinction more loudly than a grey footer line.
